runs.summary: Data through Oct 9 (Q4 7-day partial). Top 3: SMH +67.5%, CIBR +54.4%, XLE +48.4%. SPY P/E: 25.15x (P/E source frozen for 4 weeks)
runs.content:
Top 5 YTD 2026: SMH +67.5% (P/E 36.95x, Expensive), CIBR +54.4% (36.76x, Expensive), XLE +48.4% (16.95x, Fair), XLK +38.6% (34.41x, Elevated), XBI +26.2% (P/E N/A).

Bottom 5 YTD 2026: XLC -5.4% (17.15x, Fair), XLY -4.9% (25.80x, Elevated), ITA -3.5% (32.74x, Elevated), GLD -3.0% (P/E N/A), JETS -2.2% (10.37x, Cheap).

Notable shifts: Rotation within tech. SMH fell ~4.4% on the week (Q4 partial +3.6% -> -0.9%), while CIBR gained ~5% (Q4 +6.7%), cutting the gap between them from 28 to 13pp. One momentum change: JETS Fading -> Reversing (YTD now negative). XLF and KIE are back to positive YTD, so 7 sectors are negative YTD (down from 8). Defensives bounced (XLU +5.0%, XLP +3.5% in Q4); XLU and XLY stay Reversing until a full quarter confirms. SPY is +15.1% YTD, and 6 of 25 sectors beat it. No P/E band crossings: all P/Es identical for a 4th straight week, so replacing the P/E source is overdue.

runs.content:

Notable shifts: Q3 is now final. SPY rose +2.4% in Q3, but 17 of the 25 sectors fell. Three momentum downgrades: GDX Improving→Fading (YTD +8.3%→+2.4%), XLC Improving→Fading, and XLF Continuing→Fading. XLF and KIE turned YTD negative, so 8 sectors are now negative YTD. CIBR finished Q3 +14.7% (Accelerating), and SMH opened Q4 +3.6%. SPY is +13.7% YTD, and 6 of 25 sectors beat it. No P/E band crossings reported: P/Es have been identical for a third straight week, and a live check showed stockanalysis.com is still serving the same values. XLK is likely already above 35x on a live basis.
